summary: There are two defects. Total's loop starts at index 1, so it skips the first invoice line: the criterion-1 example returns 45 instead of 225. ParseQty drops strconv.Atoi's error and never checks n >= 1, so "abc" and "0" both return 0 with a nil error. The discount range check is correct and tested. Criteria 1 and 2 are unmet.

findings.title: Total skips the first invoice line
findings.detail: The loop starts at i := 1, so lines[0] is never added. For [{100, 2}, {50, 1}] with a 10% discount the sum is 50, and Total returns 45 instead of 225. Every invoice is undercharged by its first line, and a single-line invoice totals 0.
findings.fix: Iterate over every line: for _, l := range lines { sum += l.Cents * int64(l.Qty) }.

findings.title: ParseQty ignores parse errors and accepts quantities below 1
findings.detail: The Atoi error is discarded and the function always returns nil, so non-numeric input ("abc") yields 0 with no error, and "0" or negative numbers are accepted. Form input with invalid quantities flows into Total as 0 or negative line amounts, contrary to the story and criterion 2.
findings.fix: n, err := strconv.Atoi(s); if err != nil { return 0, fmt.Errorf("invoice: quantity %q is not a whole number: %w", s, err) }; if n < 1 { return 0, fmt.Errorf("invoice: quantity %d is below 1", n) }; return n, nil.

findings.title: No tests for line summation or ParseQty
findings.detail: The only test checks the discount range with nil lines. No test sums real lines or calls ParseQty, which is why both defects above pass.
findings.fix: Add tests: Total([{100,2},{50,1}], 10) == 225; ParseQty("abc") and ParseQty("0") return errors; ParseQty("3") == 3.

criteria.evidence: total.go:15 starts the loop at 1, skipping the {100, 2} line: sum 50, less 10% gives 45, not 225.
total.go:23-24 discard the Atoi error and always return nil, so ParseQty("abc") and ParseQty("0") both return 0, nil.
total.go:11-12 return an error when the discount is over 100; TestTotalDiscountRange asserts Total(nil, 101) errors.
